choices.text: C20 lipids containing a five-membered ring with two long side chains
C18 lipids containing a six-membered carbon ring
choices.why: Prostaglandins are C20 compounds, and their ring is five-membered.

choices.text: C20 lipids containing a six-membered, oxygen-containing ring
choices.why: That ring belongs to the thromboxanes, a different class of eicosanoids.

choices.text: Acyclic C20 lipids with no ring at all
choices.why: That describes the leukotrienes. Prostaglandins have a five-membered ring.

explanation: Prostaglandins are a group of C20 lipids that contain a five-membered ring with two long side chains.

prompt: Where does the name prostaglandin come from?

choices.text: The compounds were first isolated from sheep prostate glands
The compounds are found only in the prostate gland
choices.why: They have since been found in small amounts in all body tissues and fluids. The name reflects only where they were first isolated.

choices.text: The compounds are made from prostanoic acid in the liver
choices.why: The section derives the name from the sheep prostate glands where they were first found.

choices.text: The compounds were first made synthetically at the Karolinska Institute
choices.why: Ulf von Euler first isolated them from a natural source, sheep prostate glands.

explanation: The name prostaglandin derives from the fact that the compounds were first isolated from sheep prostate glands, but they have since been found in small amounts in all body tissues and fluids.

prompt: Which of these is one of the biological effects of prostaglandins listed in the section?

choices.text: Stimulating uterine contractions during childbirth
Raising blood pressure
choices.why: The section says prostaglandins can lower blood pressure.

choices.text: Increasing gastric secretions
choices.why: The section says prostaglandins lower gastric secretions.

choices.text: Storing long-term energy in fat tissue
choices.why: Energy storage is the role of triacylglycerols (Section 27.1), not prostaglandins.

explanation: Prostaglandins can lower blood pressure, affect blood platelet aggregation during clotting, lower gastric secretions, control inflammation, affect kidney function, affect reproductive systems, and stimulate uterine contractions during childbirth.

prompt: From which compound are all the eicosanoids derived biologically?

choices.text: Arachidonic acid, 5,8,11,14-eicosatetraenoic acid
Linolenic acid, an omega-3 fatty acid
choices.why: Linolenic acid has 18 carbons. The C20 eicosanoids come from the C20 arachidonic acid.

choices.text: Oleic acid
choices.why: Oleic acid is a C18 monounsaturated fatty acid. The C20 eicosanoids come from the C20 arachidonic acid.

choices.text: Phosphatidic acid
choices.why: Phosphatidic acid is the parent of the glycerophospholipids (Section 27.3).

explanation: Prostaglandins, thromboxanes, and leukotrienes are called eicosanoids because they are derived biologically from 5,8,11,14-eicosatetraenoic acid, or arachidonic acid.

prompt: How do the ring systems of prostaglandins (PG), thromboxanes (TX), and leukotrienes (LT) differ?

choices.text: PG: a cyclopentane ring; TX: a six-membered, oxygen-containing ring; LT: no ring
PG: a six-membered, oxygen-containing ring; TX: a cyclopentane ring; LT: no ring
choices.why: The rings of prostaglandins and thromboxanes are swapped here.

choices.text: PG: a cyclopentane ring; TX: no ring; LT: a six-membered, oxygen-containing ring
choices.why: The leukotrienes are the acyclic ones; the thromboxanes have the oxygen-containing ring.

choices.text: All three have a cyclopentane ring and differ only in their side chains
choices.why: The ring system is what distinguishes the three classes; leukotrienes have no ring at all.

explanation: Prostaglandins have a cyclopentane ring with two long side chains, thromboxanes have a six-membered, oxygen-containing ring, and leukotrienes are acyclic.

prompt: In eicosanoid names, the subscript gives the number of double bonds; for example, PGE1 has the E substitution pattern and one double bond. How many double bonds does leukotriene E4 (LTE4) have?
explanation: The letters PG, TX, or LT give the ring system, a letter gives the substitution pattern, and the subscript gives the number of double bonds. LTE4 therefore has 4 double bonds.

prompt: Eicosanoids are numbered the same way as arachidonic acid, starting with the –CO2H carbon as carbon 1. What number does the –CH3 carbon at the other end of the chain get?
explanation: The numbering starts with the –CO2H carbon as carbon 1, continues around the ring, and ends with the –CH3 carbon at the other end of the chain as carbon 20, since eicosanoids are C20 compounds.

prompt: What is the role of COX-2, as distinct from COX-1?

choices.text: It produces additional prostaglandin in response to arthritis or other inflammatory conditions
It carries out the normal physiological production of prostaglandins
choices.why: That is the role of COX-1.

choices.text: It catalyzes a different reaction that converts PGH2 into PGE2
choices.why: COX-1 and COX-2 accomplish the same reaction, arachidonic acid to PGH2. PGE2 forms from PGH2 by PGE synthase.

choices.text: It breaks prostaglandins down into arachidonic acid
choices.why: Both COX enzymes make prostaglandins from arachidonic acid; they don't break them down.

explanation: PGHS-1 and PGHS-2 (COX-1 and COX-2) accomplish the same reaction but function independently. COX-1 carries out normal physiological production of prostaglandins, and COX-2 produces additional prostaglandin in response to arthritis or other inflammatory conditions. Drugs such as Vioxx and Bextra selectively inhibit COX-2.

prompt: What two transformations does PGH synthase (PGHS) carry out?

choices.text: Reaction of arachidonic acid with O2 to give PGG2, then reduction of its hydroperoxide group (–OOH) to the alcohol PGH2
Reduction of arachidonic acid to PGG2, then oxidation of PGG2 with O2 to give PGH2
choices.why: The order is reversed: O2 reacts first to give PGG2, and then the –OOH group is reduced to give PGH2.

choices.text: Isomerization of arachidonic acid to PGH2, then isomerization of PGH2 to PGE2
choices.why: The first step uses O2, and the conversion of PGH2 to PGE2 is done by a different enzyme, PGE synthase.

choices.text: Hydrolysis of a phospholipid to give arachidonic acid, then cyclization to PGH2
choices.why: The section doesn't describe these as PGHS reactions. PGHS reacts arachidonic acid with O2 and then reduces the hydroperoxide.

explanation: PGHS accomplishes two transformations: an initial reaction of arachidonic acid with O2 to yield PGG2 and a subsequent reduction of the hydroperoxide group (–OOH) to the alcohol PGH2.

prompt: How does PGE2 arise from PGH2?

choices.text: By an isomerization catalyzed by PGE synthase (PGES)
By a reaction with O2 catalyzed by cyclooxygenase
choices.why: Cyclooxygenase (PGHS) makes PGH2 from arachidonic acid. The next step, PGH2 to PGE2, is an isomerization by PGE synthase.

choices.text: By hydrogenation over a nickel catalyst
choices.why: That is how vegetable oils are hardened (Section 27.1), not a biological step.

choices.text: By loss of CO2 from PGH2
choices.why: PGE2 and PGH2 are both C20 compounds; the conversion is an isomerization, with no carbon lost.

explanation: Further processing of PGH2 leads to other eicosanoids. PGE2, for instance, arises by an isomerization of PGH2 catalyzed by PGE synthase (PGES), as shown in Figure 27.4.3.
